body.text: Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharājasūtram |
body.translated_text: <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharājasūtra</s> (The Sūtra of the Medicine Master, King of Lapis Lazuli Radiance)

body.text: oṃ namaḥ sarvajñāya | namo bhagavate bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharājāya tathāgatāya ||
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Homage to the Omniscient One. Homage to the <s>Bhagavat</s>, the Medicine Master, King of Lapis Lazuli Radiance, the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān janapadacaryāṃ caramāṇo 'nupūrveṇa yena vaiśālī mahānagarī tenānuprāpto 'bhūt | tatra khalu bhagavān vaiśālyāṃ viharati sma vādyasvaravṛkṣamūle mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham aṣṭabhirbikṣusahasraiḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadbhiś ca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ rājāmātyabrāhmaṇagṛhapatisaṃhatyā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaparṣadā ca parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayati sma | atha khalu mañjuśrīr dharmarājaputro buddhānubhāvenotthāyāsanād ekaṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam etad avocat - deśayatu bhagavaṃs teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ nāmāni, teṣāṃ pūrvapraṇidhānavistaravibhaṅgam | vayaṃ śrutvā sarvakarmāvaraṇāni viśodhayema paścime kāle paścime samaye saddharmapratirūpake vartamāne sattvānām anugraham upādāya | atha bhagavān mañjuśriye kumārabhūtāya sādhukāram adāt - sādhu sādhu mañjuśrīḥ, mahākāruṇikas tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ | tvam aprameyāṃ karuṇāṃ janayitvā samādhesase(?) nānākarmāvaraṇenāvṛtānāṃ sattvānām arthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca hitārthāya | tena hi tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye | evaṃ bhagavan, iti mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt | bhagavāṃs tasyaitad avocat -
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavat</s>, wandering through the countryside, arrived in due course at the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. There the <s>Bhagavat</s> was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s> at the foot of the musical-sound tree, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, eight thousand <s>bhikṣus</s>, and thirty-six thousand <s>bodhisattvas</s>, together with a company of kings, ministers, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders, and surrounded and attended by an assembly of <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans and non-humans, he was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the Prince of the Dharma, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and bowing with joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavat</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavat</s> teach the names of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> and the detailed exposition of their former vows (<s>pūrvapraṇidhāna</s>). Having heard, we would purify all <s>karmāvaraṇas</s> (obscurations of action), for the benefit of beings living in the latter time, the latter age, when the semblance of the True <s>Dharma</s> prevails.' Then the <s>Bhagavat</s> gave his approval to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful one: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>! You are of great compassion, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>. Having generated immeasurable compassion, you exhort [me] for the sake, benefit, and happiness of beings enveloped by various <s>karmāvaraṇas</s>, and for the benefit of <s>devas</s> and humans. Therefore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, listen well and attend carefully; I shall speak.' 'So be it, <s>Bhagavat</s>,' thus <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful one, assented to the <s>Bhagavat</s>. The <s>Bhagavat</s> spoke to him thus:

body.text: asti mañjuśrīḥ pūrvasmin digbhāge ito buddhakṣetrād daśagaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy atikramya vaidūryanirbhāsā nāma lokadhātuḥ | tatra bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho viharati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiś ca śāstā devānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān| tasya khalu punar mañjuśrīḥ bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacārikāṃ carata imāni dvādaśa mahāpraṇidhānāny abhūvan | katamāni dvādaśa mahāpraṇidhānāni? prathamaṃ tasya mahāpraṇidhānam abhūt yadāham anāgate 'dhvani anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyeyam, tadā mama śarīraprabhayā aprameyāsaṃkhyeyāparimāṇā lokadhātavo bhrājeraṃs tapyeran viroceran | yathā cāhaṃ dvātriṃśadbhir mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataḥ, aśītibhiś cānuvyañjanair alaṃkṛtadehaḥ, tathaiva sarvasattvā bhaveyuḥ || (dvitīyaṃ tasya mahāpraṇidhānam abhūt - yadāham anāgate 'dhvani anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbudhyeyam, tadā bodhiprāptasya ca me kāyaḥ anarghavaidūryamaṇir iva antarbahiratyantapariśuddho vimalaprabhāsaṃpannaḥ syāt | vipulakāyas tadupamena śriyā tejasā ca pratyupasthitaḥ syāt | tasyāṃśujālāni raviśaśikarānatikrameyuḥ te ca ye kecit sattvā lokadhātau jātāś ca, ye cāpi puruṣāḥ, te tamisrāyāṃ ratrāvandhakāre nānādiśaṃ gaccheyuḥ | sarvadikṣu mama ābhayāṃ spṛṣṭāḥ kuśalāni ca) karmāṇi kurvīran || tṛtīyaṃ tasya mahāpraṇidhānam abhūt - (

children.translated_text: "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, may those beings, through the empowerment of immeasurable wisdom and skillful means (<s>prajñopāya</s>), serve for the inexhaustible enjoyment and use of the boundless realm of beings. May no being suffer any deficiency whatsoever." This was his fourth great vow (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>). "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, may those beings who have entered the wrong path, those who have entered the path of the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and those who have entered the path of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — may all those beings be established on the supreme path to awakening, in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>." This was his fifth great vow. "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, may all those beings who practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in my teaching be of unbroken moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), well-restrained. And may no one whose moral conduct has lapsed, upon hearing my name, ever go to any evil destiny." This was his sixth great vow. "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, may those beings who have inferior bodies, impaired faculties, ugly complexion, who are dull, stammering, mute, lame, hunchbacked, leprous, one-handed, blind, deaf, insane, and who suffer from other bodily diseases — upon hearing my name, may they all become whole in their faculties, with perfectly complete limbs." This was his seventh great vow. "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, may those beings who are afflicted by various diseases, who are without protector, without refuge, bereft of medicine and supplies, who are destitute, poor, and suffering — if my name should fall upon their ears, may all their diseases be pacified, and may they be free from illness and free from calamity until the attainment of <s>bodhi</s>." This was his eighth great vow. "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, whatever woman, afflicted by hundreds of faults pertaining to womanhood, disgusted with the despised state of being a woman and wishing to be freed from female birth, should hold my name — for that woman, there shall be no more female existence until the attainment of <s>bodhi</s>." This was his ninth great vow. "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, I shall turn all beings who are bound by the bonds of <s>Māra</s>'s snare, who have fallen into the thicket and straits of various wrong views — turning them away from all <s>Māra</s>'s snares, wrong views, and evil courses, establishing them in right view, and gradually revealing to them the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice." This was his tenth great vow. "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, may whatever beings are frightened by the terrors of kings, or who are bound in prison, condemned to death, harassed by various deceits, humiliated, and tormented by bodily, verbal, and mental suffering — upon hearing my name, by the power of my merit, may they be freed from all fears and calamities." This was his eleventh great vow. "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, may those beings who are burning with the fire of hunger, engaged in seeking food and drink, and who commit evil on that account — if they should hold my name, I shall satisfy their bodies with food endowed with excellent color, fragrance, and taste." This was his twelfth great vow. "When I in the future [attain supreme awakening] — then, upon my attaining <s>bodhi</s>, whatever beings are poor, bereft of clothing, tormented by cold, heat, gadflies, and mosquitoes, experiencing suffering day and night — if they should hold my name, I shall provide them with garments for their use, and offer them various pleasures dyed in many colors,

children.text: ) vividhaiś ca ratnābharaṇagandhamālyavilepanavādyatūryatālāvacaraiḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sarvābhiprāyān paripūrayeyam || imāni dvādaśa mahāpraṇidhānāni mañjuśrīḥ bhagavān bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhas tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ pūrvaṃ bodhicārikāṃ caran kṛtavān ||
children.translated_text: and with various ornaments of jewels, garlands of incense, ointments, and with musical instruments, drums, and cymbals, may I fulfill all the wishes of all beings.' These twelve great vows, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, were made by the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, when formerly practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> path.

body.translated_text: There is, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, in the eastern direction from this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), beyond Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of ten Ganges rivers, a world-system called <s>Vaidūryanirbhāsā</s> (Lapis Lazuli Radiance). There the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> (Medicine Master of Lapis Lazuli Radiance), the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, dwells—endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Persons to be Tamed, Teacher of <s>Devas</s> and Humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Now, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, when that <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> was formerly practicing the <s>bodhisattva</s> path, he made these twelve great vows (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>). What are these twelve great vows? The first of his great vows was: 'When in a future age I attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), may immeasurable, countless, boundless world-systems shine, blaze, and radiate with the light of my body. And just as I am endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) and adorned with eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), so too may all beings become.' (The second of his great vows was: 'When in a future age I attain unsurpassed perfect awakening, may my body upon attaining awakening be like a priceless lapis lazuli gem, utterly pure within and without, endowed with immaculate radiance, a vast body attended by such splendor and brilliance. May its rays of light surpass the rays of the sun and moon. And whatever beings are born in that world-system, and whatever persons there are, when they walk in the darkness of the night, may they be touched by my radiance in all directions and) perform wholesome deeds.' The third of his great vows was: (

body.text: tasya khalu punar mañjuśrīḥ bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya yat praṇidhānaṃ yac ca buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaṃ tan na śakyaṃ kalpena vā kalpāvaśeṣeṇa vā kṣapayitum | suviśuddhaṃ tad buddhakṣetraṃ vyapagataśilāśarkarakaṭhalyam apagatakāmadoṣam apagatāpāyaduḥkhaśabdam apagatamātṛgrāmam | vaidūryamayī ca sā mahāpṛthivī kuḍyaprākāraprāsādatoraṇagavākṣajālaniryūhasaptaratnamayī, yadṛśī sukhāvatī lokadhātus tādṛśī | tatra vaidūryanirbhāsāyāṃ lokadhātau dvau bodhisattvau mahāsattvau teṣām aprameyāṇām asaṃkhyeyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pramukhau, ekakaḥ sūryavairocano nāma, dvitīyaś candravairocanaḥ, yau tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya saddharmakośaṃ dhārayataḥ | tasmāt tarhi mañjuśrīḥ śrāddhena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā tatra buddhakṣetropapattaye praṇidhānaṃ karaṇīyam ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the vows of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, and the array of the qualities of his <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), cannot be exhausted in a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon) or even in the remainder of a <s>kalpa</s>. That <s>buddhakṣetra</s> is perfectly pure, free from stones, gravel, and hardness, free from the taints of desire, free from the sounds of suffering and the lower realms of existence, free from womankind. That great earth is made of lapis lazuli, with walls, ramparts, palaces, gateways, lattice windows, and canopied balconies made of the seven precious substances—just like the world-system <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (the Realm of Bliss). In that world-system <s>Vaidūryanirbhāsā</s>, there are two <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s> who are the foremost among those immeasurable, countless <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>: the first is named <s>Sūryavairocana</s> (Sun-Radiance), and the second <s>Candravairocana</s> (Moon-Radiance), who uphold the treasury of the True <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a faithful son or daughter of good family should make a vow to be reborn in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam āmantrayate sma - santi mañjuśrīḥ pṛthagjanāḥ sattvāḥ, ye na jānanti kuśalākuśalaṃ karma | te lobhābhibhūtā ajānanto dānaṃ dānasya ca mahāvipākam, bālāgramūrkhāḥ śraddhendriyavikalā dhanasaṃcayakṣaṇābhiyuktāḥ | na ca dānasaṃvibhāge teṣāṃ cittaṃ kramate | dānakāle upasthite svaśarīramaṃsacchedane iva vā manaso (duḥkhaṃ) bhavati | aneke ca sattvāḥ ye svayam eva na paribhuñjanti, prāgeva mātāpitṛbhāryāduhitṝṇāṃ dāsyanti, prāgeva dāsadāsīkarmakarāṇām, prāgevānyeṣāṃ yācakānām, te tādṛśāḥ sattvā itaś cyutvā pretaloke upapatsyante tiryagyonau vā | yaiḥ pūrvaṃ manuṣyabhūtaiḥ śrutaṃ bhaviṣyati tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyam, tatra teṣāṃ yamalokasthitānāṃ tiryagyonisthitānāṃ vā tasya tathāgatasya nāma su(saṃ?)mukhībhaviṣyati | saha smaraṇamātreṇa ataś cyutvā punar api manuṣyaloke upapatsyante, jātismarāś ca bhaviṣyanti | te te durgatibhayabhītā na bhūyaḥ kāmaguṇebhir arthikā bhaviṣyanti, dānābhiratāś ca bhaviṣyanti dānasya ca varṇavādinaḥ | sarvam api parityāgenānupūrveṇa karacaraṇaśīrṣanayanaṃ ca māṃsaśoṇitaṃ (ca) yācakānām anupradāsyanti, prāgeva anyaṃ dhanaskandham ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful one: 'There are, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, ordinary beings who do not know wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>. Overcome by greed, not knowing generosity (<s>dāna</s>) nor the great ripening of generosity, they are foolish, ignorant, and dull, lacking the faculty of faith, devoted to accumulating wealth. The thought of sharing through generosity does not arise in their minds. When the time for giving comes, their minds experience suffering as if cutting the flesh of their own bodies. And there are many beings who do not enjoy [their wealth] even themselves, let alone giving to mothers, fathers, wives, and daughters, let alone to male and female servants and laborers, let alone to other beggars. Such beings, having departed from this [life], will be reborn in the <s>pretaloka</s> (realm of hungry ghosts) or in animal births. But those who, when formerly human, shall have heard the name of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>—for them, even while abiding in the realm of <s>Yama</s> (the world of the dead) or in animal births, the name of that <s>Tathāgata</s> will come to mind. By the mere act of remembering, having departed from there, they will again be reborn in the human world with memory of their past lives. Being terrified by the fear of evil destinies, they will no longer desire the pleasures of the senses; they will delight in generosity and speak in praise of generosity. Progressively through complete renunciation, they will give even their hands, feet, head, eyes, flesh, and blood to beggars, let alone other heaps of wealth.'

body.text: punar aparaṃ mañjuśrīḥ santi sattvāḥ ye tathāgatānuddiśya śikṣāpadāni dhārayanti, te śīlavipattim āpadyante, dṛṣṭivipattim ācāravipattiṃ vā kadācid āpadyante | śīlavipannā ye punaḥ śīlavanto bhavanti, śīlaṃ rakṣanti, na punar bahuśrutaṃ paryeṣyanti, na ca tathāgatabhāṣitānāṃ gambhīram artham ājānanti | ye ca punar buhuśrutāḥ, te ādhimānikā bhaviṣyanti mānastabdhāḥ, pareṣām īrṣyāparāyaṇāḥ saddharmam avamanyante pratikṣipanti | mārapakṣikās te tādṛḥā mohapuruṣāḥ svayaṃ kumārgapratipannāḥ | anyāni cānekāni sattvakoṭiniyutaḥatasahasrāṇi mahāprapāte prapātayanti | teṣām evaṃrūpāṇāṃ sattvānāṃ bhūyiṣṭhena narakavāsagatir bhaviṣyati | tatra (

children.text: ) yais tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ ḥrutaṃ bhaviṣyanti, teṣāṃ tatra narake sthitānāṃ buddhānubhāvena tasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ sumukhībhaviṣyati | te tataḥ cyutvā punar api manuṣyaloke upapatsyante samyagdṛṣṭisaṃpannā vīryavantaḥ kalyāṇāḥayāḥ | te gṛhān utsṛjya tathāgataḥāsane pravrajitvā ānupūrveṇa bodhisattvacārikāṃ paripūrayiṣyanti ||
children.translated_text: Those who will have heard the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, while stationed in that hell — by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s>'s name will come to the forefront of their minds. Having passed away from there, they will again be reborn in the human world, endowed with right view, energetic, and of good conduct. They, abandoning the household life and going forth into the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching, will gradually fulfill the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there are beings who, having taken training rules directed toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, fall into moral failure (<s>śīlavipatti</s>); some fall into wrong view or wrong conduct. Those with failed morality who then become moral and guard their morality, they do not seek great learning nor understand the profound meaning of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s words. And those who are learned become conceited, stiff with pride, given to jealousy toward others; they disparage and reject the True <s>Dharma</s>. Such deluded persons, partisans of <s>Māra</s>, themselves treading the wrong path, cast many hundreds of thousands of millions of beings into the great precipice. For such beings, the destiny of hell will predominantly be their lot. Therein (

body.text: punar aparaṃ mañjuśrīḥ santi sattvāḥ ye ātmano varṇaṃ bhāṣante matsariṇaḥ, pareṣām avarṇam uccārayanti | ātmotkarṣakaparapaṃsakāḥ sattvāḥ parasparasatkṛtvāḥ tryapāyeṣu bahūni varṣasahasrāṇi duḥkham anubhaviṣyanti | te anekavarṣasahasrāṇām atyayena tataś cyutvā gavāśvoṣṭragardabhādiṣu tiryagyoniṣu upapadyante | kaśādaṇḍaprahāreṇa tāḍitāḥ kṣuttarṣapīḍitaśarīrā mahāntaṃ bhāraṃ vahamānā mārgaṃ gacchanti | yadi kadācit manuṣyajanmapratilābhaṃ pratilapsyante, te nityakālaṃ nīcakuleṣu upapatsyante, dāsatve ca paravaśagatā bhaviṣyanti | yaiḥ pūrvaṃ manuṣyabhūtais tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ śrutaṃ bhaviṣyati, te tena kuśalamūlena sarvaduḥkhebhyaḥ parimokṣyante, tīkṣṇendriyāś ca bhaviṣyanti paṇḍitā vyaktā meghāvinaś ca | kuśalaparyeṣṭyabhiyuktā nityaṃ ca kalyāṇamitrasamavadhānaṃ lapsyante, mārapāśam ucchidya avidyāṇḍakośaṃ bhindanti, kleśanadīm ucchoṣayanti, jātijarāvyādhimaraṇabhayaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ parimucyanti ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there are beings who praise their own virtues and are envious, who decry the virtues of others — self-exalting and other-disparaging beings. Such beings, having engaged in mutual hostility, will experience suffering for many thousands of years in the three evil destinies (<s>tryapāya</s>). After the passage of many thousands of years, having passed away from there, they are reborn in animal births (<s>tiryagyoni</s>) such as cattle, horses, camels, donkeys, and the like. Struck with whips, rods, and blows, their bodies tormented by hunger and thirst, they travel the road bearing great burdens. If at some time they regain a human birth, they will always be reborn in low families, subjected to servitude and under the power of others. Those who, when formerly human, will have heard the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> — by that root of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), they will be liberated from all sufferings and will become sharp in faculties, wise, discerning, and intelligent. Always devoted to the pursuit of the wholesome, they will constantly obtain the company of spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). They will cut through <s>Māra</s>'s snare, shatter the eggshell of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), dry up the river of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and become freed from birth, old age, disease, death, fear, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress.

body.text: punar aparaṃ mañjuśrīḥ santi sattvāḥ ye paiśunyābhiratāḥ sattvānāṃ parasparaṃ kalahavigrahavivādān kārāpayanti | te parasparaṃ vigrahacittāḥ sattvā nānāvidhamakuśalam abhisaṃskurvanti kāyena vācā manasā, anyonyam ahitakāmā nityaṃ parasparam anarthāya parākrāmanti | te ca vanadevatām āvāhayanti vṛkṣadevatāṃ giridevatāṃ ca | śmaśāneṣu pṛthag bhūtān āvāhayanti | tiryagyonigatāṃś ca prāṇino jīvitād vyavaropayanti | māṃsarudhirabhakṣān yakṣarākṣasān pūjayanti | tasya śatror nāma vā śarīrapratimāṃ vā kṛtvā tatra ghoravidyāṃ sādhayanti kākhordavetālānuprayogeṇa jīvitāntarāyaṃ vā śarīravināśaṃ vā kartukāmāḥ | yaiḥ punas tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ śrutaṃ bhaviṣyati, teṣāṃ na śakyaṃ kenāntarāyaṃ kartum | sarve ca te parasparaṃ maitracittā hitacittā avyāpannacittāś ca viharanti svakasvakena parigraheṇa saṃtuṣṭāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there are beings who delight in slander (<s>paiśunya</s>) and cause quarrels, disputes, and conflicts among beings. Those beings of hostile minds create various kinds of unwholesome <s>karma</s> by body, speech, and mind, wishing harm to one another, constantly striving for each other's ruin. They invoke forest deities, tree deities, and mountain deities. In cemeteries they invoke various <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits). They kill living beings of animal birth. They worship <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> who consume flesh and blood. Having made the enemy's name or bodily effigy, they practice terrible spells there, wishing to cause the loss of life or destruction of the body through the employment of <s>kākhordas</s> (sorcerous poisons) and <s>vetālas</s> (reanimated corpses). But for those who will have heard the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, no one will be able to cause them harm. And all those beings will dwell with minds of loving-kindness (<s>maitracittā</s>) toward one another, with benevolent minds, with unmalicious minds, contented with their own possessions.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mañjuśrīḥ etāś catasraḥ parṣado bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ, ye cānye śrāddhāḥ kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā āryāṣṭāṅgaiḥ samanvāgatā upavāsam upavasanti, ekavārṣikaṃ vā traimāsikaṃ vā śikṣāpadaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, yeṣām evaṃpraṇidhānam evamabhiprāyam - anena vayaṃ kuśalamūlena paścimāyāṃ diśi sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau upapadyema yatrāmitāyus tathāgataḥ | yaiḥ punas tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ śrutaṃ bhaviṣyati, teṣāṃ maraṇakālasamaye aṣṭau bodhisattvā ṛddhyāgatā upadarśayanti, te tatra nānāraṅgeṣu padmeṣūpapādukāḥ prādurbhaviṣyanti | kecid punar devaloke upapadyante | teṣāṃ tatropapannānāṃ pūrvakaṃ (

children.text: ) kuśalamūlaṃ na kṣīyate, na ca durgatigamanaṃ bhaviṣyati | te tataś cyutvā iha manuṣyaloke upapatsyante | rājāno bhaviṣyanti caturdvīpeśvarāś cakravartinaḥ | te anekāni sattvakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi daśasu kuśaleṣu karmapatheṣu pratiṣṭhāpayiṣyanti | apare punaḥ kṣatriyamahāśālakuleṣu brāhmaṇamahāśālakuleṣu prabhūtadhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgārasamṛddheṣu ca kuleṣu upapatsyante | te rūpasaṃpannāś ca bhaviṣyanti, eśvaryasaṃpannāś ca bhaviṣyanti, parivārasaṃpannāś ca bhaviṣyanti | yaś ca mātṛgrāmaḥ tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ śrutvā ca udgrahīṣyati, tasya sa eva paścimaḥ strībhāvaḥ pratikāṅkṣitavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) their roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) will not be exhausted, nor will there be going to bad destinies (<s>durgati</s>). They, having fallen from there, will be reborn in this human world. They will become kings, lords of the four continents, <s>cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs). They will establish many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>niyutas</s>, hundreds of thousands of beings in the ten wholesome courses of action (<s>kuśala karmapathas</s>). Others will be reborn in great <s>kṣatriya</s> families, great <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families, and families abounding in wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses. They will be endowed with beauty, endowed with sovereignty, and endowed with retinue. And whatever woman (<s>mātṛgrāma</s>), having heard the name of that <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, shall retain [it] — for her, that very birth as a woman should be expected to be her last.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, these four assemblies — <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, and <s>upāsikās</s> — and other faithful sons of good family or daughters of good family who observe the <s>poṣadha</s> (fasting day) endowed with the eight noble factors, who will maintain the training precepts for one year or three months, who have this aspiration and intention: 'By this root of merit, may we be reborn in <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, the world-system in the western direction, where the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> dwells' — for those who will have heard the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, at the time of death, eight <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will appear, having come by supernatural power. atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantam etad avocat - ahaṃ bhagavan paścime kāle paścime samaye teṣāṃ śrāddhānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ śrāvayiṣyāmi, antaśaḥ svapnāntaram api buddhanāmakaṃ karṇapuṭeṣu upasaṃhārayiṣyāmi | ye idaṃ sūtraratnaṃ dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti deśayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, parebhyo vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, likhiṣyanti likhāpayiṣyanti, pustakagataṃ vā kṛtvā satkariṣyanti nānāpuṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanachatradhvajapatākābhiḥ, tat pañcaraṅgikavastraiḥ pariveṣṭya śucau pradeśe sthāpayitavyam | yatraiva idaṃ sūtrāntaṃ sthāpitaṃ bhavati, tatra catvāro mahārājānaḥ saparivārāḥ, anyāni ca anekāni ca devakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrāṇi upasaṃkramiṣyanti | tatredaṃ sūtraṃ pracariṣyati | te ca bhagavan idaṃ sūtraratnaṃ prakāśayiṣyanti | tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya pūrvapraṇidhānaviśeṣavistaravibhāgaṃ ca tasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, teṣāṃ nākālamaraṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | na teṣāṃ kenacit śakyamojo 'pahartum, hṛtaṃ vā ojaḥ punar api pratisaṃharati | bhagavān āha - etam etad mañjuśrīḥ, evam etat, yathā vadasi | yaś ca mañjuśrīḥ śrāddhaḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tasya tathāgatasya pūjāṃ kartukāmaḥ, tena tasya tathāgatasya pratimā kārāpayitavyā, sapta rātriṃdivam āryāṣṭāṅgamārgasamanvāgatena upavāsam upavasitavyam | śucinā śucim āhāraṃ kṛtvā śucau pradeśe (nānāpuṣpāṇi saṃstārya nānāgandhapradhūpite nānāvastracchatradhvajapatākāsamalaṃkṛte tasmin pṛthivīpradeśe susnātagātreṇa śucivimalavasanadhāriṇā nirmalacittena akaluṣacittena avyāpādacittena sarvasattveṣu maitracittena (upekṣācittena) sarvasattvānām antike samacittena bhavitavyam | nānātūryasaṃgītipravāditena sā tathāgatapratimā pradakṣiṇīkartavyā tasya tathāgatasya pūrṇapraṇidhānāni manasi kartavyāni | idaṃ sūtraṃ pravartayitavyam | yaṃ cetayati, yaṃ prārthayati, taṃ sarvābhiprāyaṃ paripūrayati | yadi dirgham āyuḥ kāmayate, dirghāyuṣko bhavati | yadi bhogaṃ prārthayate, bhogasamṛddho bhavati | yadi aiśvaryam abhiprārthayate, tad alpakṛcchreṇa prāpnoti | yadi putrābhilāṣī
bhavati, putraṃ pratilabhate | ye iha pāpakaṃ svapnaṃ paśyanti, yatra vāyasaḥ sthito bhavati durnimittaṃ vā, yatra amaṅgalaśataṃ vā sthitaṃ bhavati, tais tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya pūjā kartavyā | sarvaduḥsvapnadurnimittāmāṅgalyāś ca bhāvāḥ praśamiṣyanti | (

children.text: ) yeṣām agryudakaviṣaśasrapratāpacaṇḍahastisiṃhavyāghraṛkṣatarakṣudvīpikāśīviṣavṛścikaśatapadadaṃśamaśakādibhayaṃ bhavati, tais tasya tathāgatasya pūjā kartavyā | te sarvabhayebhyaḥ parimokṣyante | yeṣāṃ corabhayaṃ taskarabhayam, tais tasya tathāgatasya pūjā kartavyā ||
children.translated_text: ) Those who have fear of floodwaters, poison, weapons, fire, fierce elephants, lions, tigers, bears, hyenas, leopards, vipers, scorpions, centipedes, gadflies, mosquitoes, and the like — by them worship of that <s>Tathāgata</s> should be performed. They will be released from all fears. Those who have fear of thieves and robbers — by them worship of that <s>Tathāgata</s> should be performed.

body.translated_text: Then indeed <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the youthful prince (<s>kumārabhūta</s>), spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'I, Blessed One, in the latter time, in the latter age, will cause those faithful sons of good family and daughters of good family to hear the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>; even in their dreams I will convey the <s>Buddha</s>'s name into the cavities of their ears. Those who will retain, recite, expound, and master this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>, who will reveal it to others in detail, who will write it or have it written, or who, having put it into a book, will honor it with various flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, parasols, banners, and flags — having wrapped it in cloth of five colors, it should be placed in a pure spot. In whatever place this <s>sūtra</s> is established, there the Four Great Kings (<s>Caturmahārāja</s>) together with their retinues, and many other tens of millions, <s>niyutas</s>, and hundreds of thousands of <s>devas</s>, will approach. There this <s>sūtra</s> will circulate, and they, Blessed One, will reveal this jewel of a <s>sūtra</s>. Those who will retain the detailed and distinct account of the special former vows (<s>pūrvapraṇidhāna</s>) of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, and the name of that <s>Tathāgata</s> — for them there will be no untimely death. Their vitality (<s>ojas</s>) cannot be stolen away by anyone, and if their vitality has been stolen, it is restored to them again.' The Blessed One said: 'So it is, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, so it is, just as you say. And whatever faithful son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, desires to perform worship of that <s>Tathāgata</s> — by that person an image of that <s>Tathāgata</s> should be commissioned, and for seven days and nights one should observe the fast endowed with the eightfold noble path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>). Having taken pure food when pure, in a pure spot — having strewn various flowers, perfumed with various fragrant incense, adorned with various cloths, parasols, banners, and flags — in that spot, with body well-bathed, wearing pure and spotless garments, with a stainless mind, an undefiled mind, a mind free of malice, with a loving mind (<s>maitracitta</s>) toward all beings and an equanimous mind (<s>upekṣācitta</s>), one should remain even-minded toward all beings. With the playing of various musical instruments and songs, that image of the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be circumambulated, and the full vows of that <s>Tathāgata</s> should be brought to mind. This <s>sūtra</s> should be recited. Whatever one intends, whatever one prays for, it fulfills all that one wishes. If one desires long life, one becomes long-lived. If one prays for enjoyments, one becomes rich in enjoyments. If one prays for sovereignty, one attains it with little difficulty. If one is desirous of a son, one obtains a son. Those who here see an evil dream, where a crow has settled or an ill omen [has appeared], or where a hundred inauspicious things have occurred — by them worship of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, should be performed. And all evil dreams, ill omens, and inauspicious things will be pacified. (

body.text: punar aparaṃ mañjuśrīḥ ye śrāddhāḥ kulaputrā va kuladuhitaro vā ye yāvajjīvaṃ triśaraṇam upagṛhṇanti, ananyadevatāś ca bhavanti, ye pañca śikṣāpadāni dhārayanti, ye ca bodhisattvasaṃvaraṃ caturvaraśikṣāpadaśataṃ dhārayanti, ye punar apiraṃ niṣkrāntagṛhavāsā bhikṣavaḥ, pañcādhike dve śikṣāpadaśate dhārayanti, yā bhikṣuṇyaḥ pañcaśataśikṣāpadāni dhārayanti, ye ca yathāparigṛhītāc chikṣāsaṃvarād anyatarāc chikṣāpadāt bhraṣṭā bhavanti saced durgatibhayabhītāḥ, tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ dhārayeyuḥ, na bhūyas teṣāṃ tryapāyagamanaduḥkhaṃ pratikāṅkṣitavyam | yaś ca mātṛgrāmaḥ prasavanakāle tīvrāṃ duḥkhāṃ kharāṃ kaṭukāṃ vedanāṃ vedayati, yā tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyam anusmaret, pūjāṃ ca kuryāt, sā sukhaṃ ca prasūyate, sarvāṅgaparipūrṇaṃ putraṃ (ca) janayiṣyati abhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyas tīkṣṇendriyo buddhimān | sa ārogyasvalpābādho bhaviṣyati, na ca śakyate amanuṣyais tasya ojo 'pahartum ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, those faithful sons of good family or daughters of good family who take the Threefold Refuge (<s>triśaraṇa</s>) for their whole lives and have no other deities; those who maintain the five training precepts (<s>śikṣāpada</s>); those who maintain the <s>bodhisattva</s> vow of four hundred training precepts; those who, having gone forth from the household life as <s>bhikṣus</s>, maintain the two hundred and five training precepts; those <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> who maintain the five hundred training precepts — if any of them have lapsed from any training precept of their adopted training discipline, and if, terrified by the fear of evil destinies, they hold the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, they need no longer expect the suffering of going to the three evil destinies (<s>tryapāya</s>). And whatever woman who, at the time of childbirth, experiences intense, painful, harsh, and bitter sensations — if she remembers the name of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, and performs worship, she will give birth easily and will bear a son complete in all limbs, handsome, graceful, pleasing to behold, sharp in faculties, and intelligent. He will be healthy and free from illness, and non-human beings will be unable to steal away his vitality.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma - śraddadhāsi tvam ānanda pattīyasi yad ahaṃ tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya guṇān varṇayiṣyāmi? athavā te kāṅkṣā vā vimatir vā vicikitsā vā atra gambhīre buddhagocare? athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat - na me bhadanta bhagavan atra kāṅkṣā vā vimatir vā vicikitsā vā tathāgatabhāṣiteṣu sūtrānteṣu | tat kasya hetoḥ? nāsti tathāgatānām apariśuddhakāyavāṅbhanaḥsamudācāratā | imau bhagavan candrasūryau evaṃ maharddhikau evaṃ mahānubhāvau pṛthivyāṃ prapatetām, sa sumerur vā parvatarājaḥ sthānāc calet, na tu buddhānāṃ vacanam anyathā bhavet | kiṃ tu bhadanta santi sattvāḥ śraddhendriyavikalāḥ | idaṃ buddhagocaraṃ śrutvāṃ evaṃ vakṣyanti katham etan nāmadheyasmaraṇamātreṇa tasya tathāgatasya tāvanto guṇānuśaṃsā bhavanti? te na śraddadhanti na pattīyanti, pratikṣipanti| teṣāṃ dīrgharātram anarthāya na hitāya na sukhāya vinipātāy bhaviṣyati | bhagavān āha - asthānam ānanda anavakāśaḥ, yena tasya tathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ śrutam, tasya sattvasya durgatyapāyagamanaṃ bhavet, nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate | duḥśraddhānīyaṃ ca ānanda buddhānāṃ buddhagocaram | yat tvam ānanda śraddadhāsi pattīyasi, tathāgatasyaiṣonubhāvo draṣṭavyaḥ | abhūmir atra sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ sthāpayitvā ekajātipratibaddhān bodhisattvān mahāsattvān iti | durlabhaḥ ānanda manuṣyapratilābhaḥ, durlabhaṃ triratne śraddhāgauravam, sudurlabhaṃ tathāgatasya nāmadheyaśravaṇam | tasya bhagavatas tathāgatasya bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya ānanda bodhisattvacaryām apramāṇam, upāyakauśalyam apy apramāṇam, apramāṇaṃ cāsya praṇidhānaviśeṣavistaram | ākāṅkṣamāṇo 'haṃ tasya tathāgatasya kalpaṃ vā (

children.text: ) kalpāvaśeṣaṃ vā bodhisattvacārikāyāṃ vistaravibhaṅgaṃ nirdiśeyam | kṣīyeta ānanda alpam, na tv eva śakyaṃ tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya pūrvapraṇidhānaviśeṣavistarāntam adhigantum ||

body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Do you believe and accept, <s>Ānanda</s>, when I praise the virtues and merits of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One? Or do you have doubt, uncertainty, or perplexity regarding this profound domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>?" Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: "I have no doubt, uncertainty, or perplexity, Venerable <s>Bhagavat</s>, regarding the sūtras spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For what reason? Because there is no impurity in the conduct of body, speech, and mind of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. <s>Bhagavat</s>, these sun and moon, of such great power and might, might fall to the earth, and <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, might move from its place — but the words of the <s>Buddhas</s> would never become otherwise. However, Venerable One, there are beings who are deficient in the faculty of faith. Having heard this domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, they will speak thus: 'How can such great benefits and merits come about merely by remembering the name of that <s>Tathāgata</s>?' They neither believe nor accept, and they reject it. For them, for a long time, there will be loss, not benefit, not happiness, but downfall." The Blessed One said: "It is impossible, <s>Ānanda</s>, it cannot happen, that a being who has heard the name of that <s>Tathāgata</s> would go to evil destinies — such a thing does not exist. Hard to believe, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the sphere of <s>Buddhas</s>. That you, <s>Ānanda</s>, believe and accept — this should be seen as the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. This is beyond the domain of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, excepting the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who are bound to one more birth. Rare, <s>Ānanda</s>, is the attainment of human birth; rare is faith and respect for the Three Jewels; and exceedingly rare is hearing the name of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice of that Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is immeasurable; his skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>) are also immeasurable; and immeasurable is the detailed extent of his special vows. body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena tasyām eva parṣadi trāṇamukto nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saṃnipatito 'bhūt saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ | utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam etad avocat - bhaviṣyanti bhadanta bhagavan sattvāḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye nānāvyādhiparipīḍitā dīrghavyādhinā (kṣīṇagātrāḥ) kṣuttarṣābhyāṃ śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhā maraṇābhimukhā rorudyamānebhir mitrajñātisālohitaiḥ parivāritā andhakārāṃ diśaṃ paśyanto yamapuruṣair ākarṣyamāṇāś ca | tasya kalevare mañcaśayite vijñānaṃ yamasya dharmarājasyāgratām upanīyate | yac ca tasya sattvasya sahajānubaddham eva yat kiṃcit tena puruṣeṇa kuśalam akuśalaṃ vā kṛtaṃ bhavati, tat sarvaṃ sulikhitaṃ kṛtvā yamasya dharmarājasya upanāmyate | tadā yamo 'pi dharmarājas taṃ pṛcchati, gaṇayati yathākṛtaṃ cāsya kuśalam akuśalaṃ vā tathājñāmājñāpayati | tatra ye te mitrajñātisālohitāstasyāturasyārthāya taṃ bhagavantaṃ bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhaṃ tathāgataṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccheyuḥ, tasya ca tathāgatasya pūjāṃ kuryuḥ, sthānam etad vidyate yat tasya tad vijñānaṃ punar api pratinivarteta, svapnāntaragata ivātmānaṃ saṃjānīte | yadi vā saptame divase yadi vā (ekaviṃśatime) divase yadi vā pañcatriṃśatime divase yadi vā ekonapañcāśatime divase tasya vijñānaṃ punar api nivarteta, smṛtim upalabheta | tasya kuśalam akuśalaṃ vā karmavipākaṃ svayam eva pratyakṣaṃ bhavati | jñātvā sa jīvitahetau na kadāpi pāpam akuśalaṃ karma kariṣyati | tasmāc chrāddhena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitā vā tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya pūjā kartavyā ||
body.translated_text: At that time, in that very assembly, the <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> named <s>Trāṇamukta</s> (Freed from Danger) had assembled and was seated. Rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, bowing with joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavat</s>, he said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: 'Venerable <s>Bhagavat</s>, in the latter time, in the latter age, there will be beings afflicted by various diseases, their bodies emaciated from long illness, with throats and lips parched from hunger and thirst, facing death, surrounded by weeping friends, relatives, and kinsmen, seeing darkness in every direction, and being dragged away by the messengers of <s>Yama</s>. While his body lies upon the deathbed, his consciousness is brought before <s>Yama</s>, the Dharma King. And that being's innate companion, who has faithfully recorded whatever wholesome or unwholesome deeds have been done by that person—all of this is presented, well-recorded, to <s>Yama</s> the Dharma King. Then <s>Yama</s> the Dharma King questions and counts him, and according to whatever wholesome or unwholesome [deeds] he has done, issues his decree accordingly. If those friends, relatives, and kinsmen, for the sake of that sick person, should go for refuge to the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> and should make offerings to that <s>Tathāgata</s>, it is possible that his consciousness may return again—he perceives himself as if in a dream. Whether on the seventh day, or on the twenty-first day, or on the thirty-fifth day, or on the forty-ninth day, his consciousness may return and he obtains remembrance. The ripening of his wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> becomes directly apparent to him. Having known this, he will never again, for the sake of living, commit evil, unwholesome deeds. Therefore, a faithful son or daughter of good family should make offerings to the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānandas trāṇamuktaṃ nāma bodhisattvam etad avocat - kathaṃ kulaputra tasya bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya pūjā kartavyā? trāṇamukto bodhisattva āha - ye bhadanta ānanda mahato vyādhitaḥ parimocitukāmāḥ, tais tasyāturasyārthāya sapta divasāni āryāṣṭāṅgasamanvāgatam upavāsam upavasitavyam, bhikṣusaṃghasya ca āhārapānaiḥ sarvopakaraṇair yathāśakti pūjopasthānaṃ kartavyam | bhagavato bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya nāmadheyaṃ triṣkṛtvā rātryāṃ triṣkṛtvā divase manasi kartavyam | navacatvāriṃśadvāre idaṃ sūtram uccārayitavyam | ekonapañcāśad dīpāḥ prajvālayitavyāḥ | sapta pratimāḥ kartavyā | ekaikayā pratimayā sapta sapta dīpāḥ prajvālayitavyāḥ | ekaiko dīpaḥ śakaṭacakrapramāṇaḥ kartavyaḥ | yadi ekonacatvāriṃśatime divase āloko na kṣīyate, veditavyaṃ sarvasaṃpaditi | pañcaraṅgikāḥ patākāḥ ekonapañcāśadadhikāḥ kartavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Trāṇamukta</s>: 'How, son of good family, should offerings be made to the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>?' The <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Trāṇamukta</s> replied: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, those who wish to be freed from great illness should, for the sake of that sick person, observe the <s>poṣadha</s> (fasting day) endowed with the noble eightfold [factors] for seven days, and should make offerings and attend upon the <s>bhikṣusaṃgha</s> (monastic community) with food, drink, and all requisites to the best of their ability. The name of the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s> should be called to mind three times during the night and three times during the day. This <s>sūtra</s> should be recited forty-nine times. Forty-nine lamps should be lit. Seven images should be made; before each image, seven lamps should be lit; each lamp should be made the size of a cart-wheel. If on the forty-ninth day the light has not gone out, one should know that all success [has been achieved]. Banners of five colors, more than forty-nine in number, should be made.'

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānandas trāṇamuktaṃ bodhisattvam evam avocat - kathaṃ kulaputra parikṣīṇāyuḥ punar evābhivivardhate? trāṇamukto bodhisattva āha - nanu tvayā bhadanta ānanda tathāgatasyāntikāc chrutam - santi akālamaraṇāni | teṣāṃ pratikṣepeṇa mantrauṣadhiprayogā upadiṣṭāḥ | santi sattvā vyādhitāḥ | na ca guruko vyādhiḥ bhaiṣajyopasthāpakavirahitaḥ | yadi vā vaidyā(bhaiṣajyaṃ) kurvanti | idaṃ prathamam akālamaraṇam | dvitīyam akālamaraṇaṃ yasya rājadaṇḍena kālakriyā | tṛtīyam akālamaraṇaṃ ye 'tīva pramattāḥ pramādavihāriṇaḥ, teṣāṃ manuṣyā ojo 'paharanti | caturtham akālamaraṇaṃ ye agnidāhena kālaṃ kurvanti | pañcamaṃ cākālamaraṇaṃ ye ca udakena mriyante | ṣaṣṭhakālamaraṇaṃ ye (siṃha)vyāghravyālacaṇḍamṛgamadhyagatā vāsaṃ kalpayanti mriyante ca | saptamama kālamaraṇaṃ ye giritaṭāt prapatanti | aṣṭamam akālamaraṇaṃ ye viṣakākhordavetālānuprayogeṇa mriyante | navamam akālamaraṇaṃ ye kṣuttṛṣopahatā āhārapānam alabhamānā ārtāḥ kālaṃ kurvanti | etāni saṃkṣepato 'kālamaraṇāni tathāgateṇa nirdiṣṭāni | anyāni ca aprameyāṇy akālamaraṇāni ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> spoke thus to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Trāṇamukta</s>: 'How, O son of good family, can a lifespan that is exhausted increase again?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Trāṇamukta</s> said: 'Have you not heard from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, venerable <s>Ānanda</s> — there are untimely deaths? For their prevention, applications of <s>mantras</s> and medicines have been taught. There are beings who are ill, yet the serious illness lacks medicine or an attendant. Or if physicians prescribe [wrong] medicine — this is the first untimely death. The second untimely death is when one dies by royal punishment. The third untimely death: those who are excessively heedless, dwelling in negligence — from them, non-human beings steal their vital essence. The fourth untimely death: those who die by burning in fire. The fifth untimely death: those who die by drowning in water. The sixth untimely death: those who take up dwelling among lions, tigers, serpents, and fierce wild beasts and die. The seventh untimely death: those who fall from a mountain cliff. The eighth untimely death: those who die through the application of poison, <s>kākhordas</s> (sorcery), <s>vetālas</s> (zombies), and the like. The ninth untimely death: those who, afflicted by hunger and thirst, unable to obtain food and drink, die in distress. These are the untimely deaths taught in brief by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And there are other immeasurable untimely deaths.'

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānando bhagavantam etad avocat - ko nāmāyaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyaḥ? kathaṃ cainaṃ dhārayāmi? bhagavān āha - tena hi ānanda dharmaparyāyam idaṃ bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabhasya tathāgatasya pūrvapraṇidhānaviśeṣavistaram iti dhāraya, dvādaśānāṃ mahāyakṣasenāpatīnāṃ praṇidhānam iti dhāraya ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavat</s>: 'What, O <s>Bhagavat</s>, is the name of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the Dharma)? And how shall I retain it?' The <s>Bhagavat</s> said: 'Therefore, <s>Ānanda</s>, retain this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> as "The Detailed Exposition of the Distinguished Former Vows of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabha</s>," and retain it as "The Vow of the Twelve Great <s>Yakṣa</s> Generals."'

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān | āttamanā mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ, āyuṣmāṃś ca ānandaḥ, trāṇamukto bodhisattvaḥ, te ca bodhisattvāḥ, te ca mahāśrāvakāḥ, te ca rājāmātyabrāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ, sarvāvatī parṣat, sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandan ||
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavat</s>. Delighted, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the youthful prince, the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Trāṇamukta</s> (Liberated Protector), those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, those great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, those kings, ministers, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders, the entire assembly, and the world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavat</s>.

body.text: āryabhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharājaṃ nāma mahāyānasūtram ||
body.translated_text: [End of] the Noble <s>Āryabhaiṣajyaguruvaidūryaprabharāja</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra.
